$BNB's 24-hour swing sat at about 3.2%, well under its typical 5.2% range, that's roughly a third tighter than usual. It nudged down 0.8% to $587.31.

$SOL moved within a 4.6% band, compared with its normal 6.9% swing, so it's also somewhat tighter. The token slipped 0.5% and is now at $74.58.

$NEAR held a 7.8% range versus the usual 10.2%, again a bit tighter than normal, and it actually rose 1.3% to $3.421.

All three are just a little more confined today, nothing wild, just a tighter-than-usual day.

$BTC slipped to $62,578, down 3.76% in 24 h, after hitting a high of $65,134.81 and finding support near $62,063.

$ETH fell 3.18% to $1,767.1, its range bounded between $1,832.42 and $1,732.83.

$BNB dropped 2.77% to $580.08, trading between $598 and $575.37.

All three sat under their day-highs, volume staying solid (BTC ~18.3 k, ETH ~289.7 k, BNB ~121.4 k).

Just a steady pull-back across the board; nothing wild to write home about.

$ETH slipped a hair against $BTC, down 0.178% to 0.02803 BTC. Meanwhile $BTC fell 1.729% in USD terms. The 20-coin basket actually rose 2.256% over the same period, so altcoins are beating Bitcoin hands-down. In short: $BTC is lagging the basket, and $ETH is losing a bit of relative strength versus $BTC. Nothing wild, just the usual 24-hour shuffle.

$BTC slid to $63,573, down 2.16% in 24 h. The high hit $65,268, low sat at $63,085, and about 19,600 BTC changed hands, pushing quote volume past $1.26 B.

$ETH is at $1,772, off 2.05%. It peaked near $1,836 and found support around $1,751.4. Roughly 319 k ETH traded, giving $572 M in quote volume.

$BNB slipped just under 1% to $586.29. The day's range was $580.78-$599.42, with 134 k BNB swapping for about $79.4 M in quote volume.

All three slipped into the red, but volume stayed solid. Looks like a calm pull-back across the board.

$BTC slipped to $64,426, down 0.73% after hitting $65,447 earlier. Volume sat around 26 k BTC, pushing $1.68 B in quote flow.

$ETH fell 1.57% to $1,803, with a high of $1,844 and a low of $1,751. Over 350 k ETH changed hands, moving $632 M in USDT.

$BNB edged lower, closing at $592, a 0.34% dip from its $599 top. Trade activity hit 141 k BNB, generating $83.6 M in quote volume.

Watch the $BTC 24-hour range; a break back above $65,000 could test whether the recent pullback was just a pause.

$HYPE is hovering around $69.82, down a hair at –0.14%. Its 24-hour swing was just 4.87%, about a third tighter than the typical 8.78% range.

$BNB slipped a touch to $595.97, up 0.97% on the day. The price moved only 3.13% versus its usual 4.98%, that's a bit tighter than normal.

$ZEC held steady near $961.2, up 6.72%. The daily range clocked in at 8.01%, noticeably less than the 11.94% it normally sees.

All three are just moving inside a narrower band than usual, nothing wild.

$BTC slipped 1.8% to $63,881, hit a high of $65,534 before easing back down to a low of $63,336. Volume sat around 27.3k BTC, pushing roughly $1.77 B in quote terms.

$ETH dropped 1.35% to $1,796, touched $1,843 on the upside, and found a floor near $1,751. It traded about 336.6k ETH, moving $608 M in quote volume.

$BNB nudged down 0.58% to $588, peaked at $595.5 and lingered above $580.78. Spot volume hit 112.5k BNB, generating $66.4 M in quote.

Watch the $BTC 24-hour high-low range; any breach of the $65.5k ceiling could set the next swing direction.

$ZEC surged 5.58% to $920.85, hitting a high of $959.95 before easing back. $UNI nudged up 1.5% to $5.21, trading in a tight $5.08-$5.45 range. Meanwhile $SOXL tanked 11.44% down to $45.07, sliding from a peak of $52.71 and barely holding above $44.40. Leaders grabbed upside while the laggard ripped hard lower, just the way 24-hour swings go.

$ETH/$BTC is at 0.02831 and nudged up 0.855% against $BTC. Meanwhile $BTC itself rose 0.325% in the last 24 h. The 20-coin basket's average alt gain was 0.642%, so the whole alt set outpaced $BTC by a hair. Bottom line: $ETH is pulling a bit of strength on the BTC chart, and the broader alt crowd is doing slightly better than $BTC overall. Nothing wild, just a modest tilt toward the rest.

$ASTER surged 15.7% to $0.5756, punching up from a low of $0.4955 and ending near its $0.5788 high. $RARE wasn't far behind, climbing 10% to $0.0136 after bouncing between $0.0114 and $0.0183. Meanwhile $SOXL tumbled 15.8% to $48.85, sliding from a $59.23 peak down to $46.99. Leaders grabbed the upside, laggards took the hit, just another wild 24-hour swing.

$ETH nudged up 0.036% against $BTC, so it's gaining a hair of relative strength. $BTC itself rose 0.388% over the last 24 h. The 20-coin basket of top alts slipped 0.92% on average, leaving $BTC ahead of the pack. ETH's tiny edge on BTC is the only bright spot; the rest of the market stayed in the red. Nothing wild, just a modest BTC lead and a whisper of ETH out-performing.

$ETH is gaining a bit on $BTC, up 0.572% vs BTC's 0.43% drop. Meanwhile the 20-coin basket is ahead of Bitcoin, averaging a 2.73% rise. So BTC's underperforming both the alt basket and its main rival, while $ETH nudges ahead in the pair. Nothing wild, just $ETH tightening on $BTC and the alts taking the lead.

$BTC slipped 0.19% to $64,964, hugging the low of $63,777 after peaking at $66,132. Volume sat around 21.7 K BTC, about $1.41 B in quote. $ETH nudged down 0.08% to $1,822.58, trading between $1,773 and $1,845 with 331 K ETH changing hands ($602 M). $BNB fell 0.52% to $592.42, bounced off a $584.45 low and a $599.72 high, moving 103 K BNB ($61 M).

Watch the $BTC 24-hour range break: if price cracks below $63,700 it could test the next support level.

$BTC hovered at $64,976, up 0.69% with a high of $66,132 and low of $62,006. Volume hit ~33k BTC, showing a modest flow.

$ETH jumped 2.02% to $1,816, touched $1,845 before slipping to $1,711. Over 489k ETH traded, pushing quote volume past $876 M.

$BNB rose 2.45% to $592.9, peaked at $599.7 and found support near $566. Around 171k BNB changed hands, generating $100 M in quote volume.

Watch the $BTC intraday range around $66k-$62k; any break of that band could set the tone for the next session.

$ETH is gaining ground on $BTC, up 0.718% in the BTC-price pair, while $BTC slipped 1.644% overall. The 20-coin basket fell 0.947% on average, so Bitcoin's drop outpaced the alts. In other words, $BTC is underperforming the basket, and $ETH is nudging ahead of $BTC. Nothing wild, just a modest shift in relative strength.

$BTC slipped 2.2% to $65,480, hitting a high of $66,922 before bottoming out near $62,006. $ETH fell 3.3% to $1,832, with the day's range from $1,711 up to $1,895. $BNB dropped just under 2% to $596.6, after rallying to $608.72 and testing $566 on the low side.

Volume stayed solid: BTC traded ~41k coins (~$2.65 B), ETH pushed 619k (~$1.12 B), and BNB moved 275k (~$162 M).

Watch the $BTC 24-hour low-high spread, if it narrows back toward the $66k zone, it could set the next price anchor.

$ETH slipped against $BTC, down 0.638% to 0.02803 BTC. Meanwhile $BTC fell 2.657% in USD terms, while the 20-coin basket lagged harder, down about 6.32% on average. So BTC's still beating the alt pack, but it's losing ground to $ETH. $ETH's modest gain versus BTC barely offsets the broader sell-off across the basket. Overall a rough 24-hour grind, with everything trending lower.

$BTC slid 6.1% to $64,398, hugging its low of $64,376 after topping $68,633. Meanwhile $UNI plunged 18.2% to $4.72, barely breaking $4.72 on the way down from a high of $5.79. The big picture? Bitcoin's still dragging the market while Uni's the sharpest drop-off in the basket. Nothing wild, just a clear split between the top mover and the biggest loser.

$BNB swung hard, covering about a 9.5% range in 24 h while it usually hugs a 3.2% band, that's more than double its normal swing.

$UNI was even messier, jumping roughly 19.4% all day versus a typical 7.5% move, so it's also more than twice the usual spread.

$SOL didn't lag far behind, bouncing close to an 11.9% range compared with its average 4.8%, again, over twice the everyday volatility.

All three busted out of their normal windows; nothing else stood out today.

$SHELL's gone wild, up 52.34% to $0.02995, trading between $0.01965 and $0.05163 with almost $39 M in volume. Meanwhile $SOXLB crumbled, down 12.936% to $55.86, its range squeezed from $66.91 to $52.43 on $43 M volume. $ZEC also slipped, losing 9.058% to $885.07, bouncing between $992.98 and $876.64 with $155 M changing hands. Leaders sprinting, laggards tumbling, just the 24-hour story.

$NVDAB slipped to 161.42 USDT, down 1.507% after hitting a high of 171.59 USDT. Volume sat around 149.6 M USDT, so the move kept rolling through the night.

Sandisk's token, $SNDKB, took a deeper tumble, 861.04 USDT now, a 6.981% drop from its peak at 946.58 USDT. Trade activity was lighter, about 28.7 M USDT, but the dip held steady past regular market close.

Tesla's bStock, $TSLAB, hovered near 387.65 USDT, down 2.574% after a brief pop to 404.54 USDT. With roughly 3.34 M USDT changing hands, the price kept drifting in after hours.

All three kept moving while traditional exchanges were offline, just another 24/7 crypto-style grind.

$SPCXBUSDT slipped about 1.7% and its 24-hour swing was roughly 4.36%, noticeably tighter than its usual ~6% daily range, about a third less volatile than normal.

$PEPEUSDT dropped 2.9% and only moved around 7.73% in the last day, which is also somewhat tighter compared with its typical ~9.8% swing.

$XRPUSDT slid 2.5% and saw a 4.59% range, basically in line with its average 4.83% range, so nothing out of the ordinary there.

All three were down, but the first two kept their moves a bit more contained than they usually do.

$NEAR surged 2.4% to $3.51, hitting a high of $3.64 while volume topped $90 M. Meanwhile $BTC slipped 3.9% to $68 893, pulling back from a $71 750 peak and still churning $2 B in trade. $HYPE managed a modest 2.2% rise to $72.78, touching $75.35 on the upside. Leaders are climbing, BTC's the biggest drags. Looks like the alt-run's outpacing the king today.

$BARD surged almost 90% to $0.1625, trading near its high of $0.1799 after a wild swing from $0.0853. Meanwhile $BTC slipped 3.6% to $69,300, pulling back from a $72,288 peak and hovering close to its low of $67,568. $ETH also fell, down 1.4% at $1,964, stuck between a $2,028 top and $1,896 floor. Big volume on the leader, tiny pullbacks on the majors, just a classic 24-hour swing.

$BTC's at $68,731, down 6.9% in 24h, slipped from a high of $73,866.72 and barely nudged above $68,527.89. $ETH sits around $1,930, also down 6.1%, fell from $2,056.73 and found support near $1,917.01. $BNB traded at $632.42, lost 6.8%, peaked at $679.03 and lingered just above $630.13. Volume's still decent, $BTC around 22,265 BTC, $ETH over 317k ETH, $BNB about 164k BNB, so liquidity's there. Watch if any of these levels hold; a break back toward the day-highs could test the upside, while staying near the lows would keep the pressure on. Nothing wild, just a solid pull-back across the board.

$NVDABUSDT surged 2.89% to 166.98, punching up to a high of 168.56 while volume hit 266.9 M. $GOOGLBUSDT wasn't far behind, climbing 2.889% to 299.55 and topping out at 302.79 on 22.9 M quote volume. Meanwhile $NEARUSDT slipped 6.601% to 3.396, barely breaking its low of 3.341 and trading 69.9 M in volume. The leaders are charging ahead, the laggard is pulling back hard. Just a quick snapshot of who's riding the wave and who's getting left in the wake.

$NVDAB is sitting at 164.97 USDT, down 5.97% after hitting a high of 176 and a low of 149.23. Volume's hefty at 276.3 M USDT, so the pullback's well-filled even though the market's asleep.

S&P 500 ETF's token $SPYB barely budged, 759.69 USDT with a 0.12% dip. The range stayed tight, high 763.55, low 753.8, and 1.85 M USDT traded, proof the bStock keeps moving 24/7 while the floor's closed.

Sandisk's $SNDKB dropped 5.88% to 935.12 USDT, swinging from a 998.7 high down to 870.83. Still, 32.8 M USDT swapped hands, showing the token's liquidity survives the off-hours grind.

All three bStocks are doing their thing around the clock, no big surprises, just the usual after-hours flow.

$BTC slipped to $71,652.98, down 2.56% in 24 h, after hitting a high of $74,811.45 and testing the low at $71,293.23. $ETH is at $2,006.51, off 2.28%, with a swing between $2,103.78 and $1,983.82. $BNB fell hardest, sitting at $653.34, down 4.00% after a brief pop to $689.30 and barely breaking $650.01. Volume's still decent, $BTC traded about 15,871 BTC, $ETH moved roughly 250 k, $BNB around 122 k. Keep an eye on whether $BNB can hold above $650; $BTC and $ETH look set to linger near today's lows. Just a flat-lined morning across the board.

$SNDKBUSDT jumped 4.7% to $947.7, carving out a tight range between $897.6 and $1,011.1 with almost $79.2 M in quote volume. $GRAMUSDT nudged up 3.1% to $1.18, holding a band from $1.127 to $1.257 and pulling in $27.2 M. Meanwhile $PEPEUSDT slumped 14.9% to $0.00000457, skidding between $0.0000045 and $0.00000537 while still racking up $79.5 M of volume. One side's pushing higher, the other's getting hammered.

$BTC slipped to $73,586, down 0.19% after peaking at $74,811. The dip stayed within a tight $73,209-$74,811 range, volume around 16.2k.

$ETH slid to $2,042, a 0.45% drop, after testing $2,104 earlier. It bounced off $2,035-$2,104 lows-highs, with roughly 191k trades moving $395M.

$BNB barely budged, holding $678.07, up 0.07% from yesterday. It hovered between $676.77 and $689.30, 78k volume pushing $53.8M.

All three sat near their 24-hour lows, no big breaks. Keep an eye on whether any token cracks the upper edge of its range.
